environmentVariables.name: RAG_GROUPING

environmentVariables.description: Maximum number of files to keep in search results. Results are filtered to include only chunks from the top N best-scoring files. For example, 1 returns only the single best-matching file's chunks. Unset means no file filtering.

environmentVariables.description: Minimum chunk length in characters (1-10000, defaults to 50). Chunks shorter than this threshold are filtered out during ingestion.

environmentVariables.description: Execution device for the embedder (defaults to cpu). Passed straight to ONNX Runtime; see the Transformers.js device source for the supported backend names. If the requested device fails to initialize, the server throws an error.

environmentVariables.description: Embedding quantization dtype for the embedder (defaults to fp32). Opt-in and pass-through; accepts any dtype the chosen model provides (fp32, fp16, q8, int8, ...). If the model has no variant for the requested dtype, the server throws an error. Changing this changes the embedding space — re-ingest existing data.
environmentVariables.name: RAG_DTYPE

environmentVariables.description: Keyword boost factor for hybrid search (0.0-1.0, defaults to 0.6). 0 means semantic similarity only; higher values increase the keyword-match contribution to the final score.

environmentVariables.description: Enable automatic file watcher to detect changes and re-index modified files (true/1 to enable). Useful during active development.

environmentVariables.name: MCP_AUTH_USER_KEY

environmentVariables.description: Interface the HTTP transport binds to. Default 127.0.0.1 (localhost only). Set 0.0.0.0 to expose on all interfaces (containers do this automatically).
environmentVariables.name: MCP_HTTP_HOST

environmentVariables.description: Maximum accepted POST /mcp request-body size in bytes (default 16777216 = 16 MiB — sized so base64 file uploads within the documented tool limits fit). Oversized requests get a 413 JSON-RPC error before/while reading — closes a memory-exhaustion DoS vector in public deployments. Note: base64 file sources are capped by this limit BEFORE MCP_FILE_MAX_BYTES applies.

environmentVariables.description: Set to "true" for public/multi-tenant deployments. environmentVariables.description: Client ID this server presents to the introspection endpoint above (its resource-server credentials). Only needed alongside MCP_SVC_INTROSPECT_URL; it does not authenticate you to EAD Enterprise Suite.

environmentVariables.description: Client secret this server presents to the introspection endpoint above (its resource-server credentials). environmentVariables.description: RFC 7662 token introspection URL for inbound Bearer verification in HTTP mode. Opt-in, and required when MCP_HTTP_PUBLIC=true. Leave empty for stdio (local) use.

environmentVariables.description: HTTP port when running in hosted (HTTP) mode; ignored in stdio mode

environmentVariables.description: Register the mutating tools. Off by default, and the gate decides whether the write tools exist at all rather than merely refusing — an agent with writes off cannot see them.
environmentVariables.name: APPLE_SAFARI_ALLOW_WRITES

environmentVariables.description: Return one-time codes: a one-time-code field in apple_safari_page_elements, and apple_safari_find_codes for a code a page shows as text. Its own gate rather than allowWrites, because it is a read. Credential fields stay redacted whatever this says.
environmentVariables.name: APPLE_SAFARI_ALLOW_CODES

environmentVariables.description: Register apple_safari_network_record, _list and _get, which record what a page you allowed the extension on fetches and read the responses. Its own gate rather than allowWrites, because it is a read; off means the tools do not exist. Headers named like credentials are masked, bodies are not. Reloading a tab to record and saving a body to a file still need APPLE_SAFARI_ALLOW_WRITES.
environmentVariables.name: APPLE_SAFARI_ALLOW_NETWORK

environmentVariables.description: Where apple_safari_network_get's saveAs writes a file. Defaults to ~/Downloads. A name is kept to its basename and an existing file is never replaced unless asked.
environmentVariables.name: APPLE_SAFARI_DOWNLOAD_DIR

environmentVariables.description: Characters of a body the server asks the page for per command when it reads a large body. Defaults to 262144, which was measured to work; how far above that Safari's native-message channel goes is unmeasured.
environmentVariables.name: APPLE_SAFARI_NETWORK_CHUNK_CHARS
